The use of prognostic and/or predictive biomarkers in patients with advanced gastric cancer is increasing.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many biomarkers that are prognostic for advanced gastric cancer (AGC) and a smaller number that are predictive for benefit from treatment.
we can now use biomarkers to identify patients who will not benefit from chemotherapy and can avoid the side effects and cost of treatment in these patients.

the prognostic and the predictive biomarkers of gastric cancer (GC) are not only important to identify the patients who will benefit from the treatment and to predict the response to treatment, but also they can be used to stratify patients into risk groups for better management and to identify patients who are at higher risk of developing recurrence and metastasis.
